newsitem.title: USA: Police interview slain Colorado girl's grandparents.
newsitem.headline: Police interview slain Colorado girl's grandparents.

text.p: Police investigating the murder of 6-year-old beauty pageant winner JonBenet Ramsey interviewed the child's maternal grandparents on Friday, while her mother and father returned home to Colorado, officials said.

Two detectives, part of a five-member investigative team from Boulder, Colo., remained for nearly four hours in the home of Don and Nedra Paugh, whose granddaughter was found strangled to death on Dec. 26.

John and Patricia Ramsey, the parents of the former Little Miss Colorado, spent part of the week in seclusion at the Paugh's after burying their daughter in nearby Marietta, Ga., on Tuesday. The family lived in Atlanta before moving to Boulder in 1991.

The Colorado detectives, one carrying a silver box believed to contain recording equipment, entered the spacious brick home of Patricia Ramsey's parents on Friday morning as a crowd of reporters watched from across the street.
"The investigators are there conducting interviews," said Sgt. Dennis Nelson of the Roswell City Police Department, which was providing the Colorado team with office space and other assistance.
"At that residence, they would be interviewing the grandparents. But they have interviewed many, many people."
Boulder Det. Steve Thomas later told reporters no arrests were pending and no search warrants were being served.
The Colorado team, which began gathering evidence in the Atlanta area Thursday, is expected back in Colorado Monday, a spokeswoman for the Boulder police said.

The body of the little girl, gagged with duct tape, was discovered in the basement of her parents' home in Boulder. Eight hours before the discovery, Patricia Ramsey had telephoned police to say she found a note claiming her daughter had been kidnapped and demanding a $118,000 ransom.
The Denver Post on Friday quoted a source close to the investigation as saying the girl had been sexually assaulted the night she was murdered.

At a news briefing, Boulder authorities remained tight-lipped to protect the integrity of the investigation. "There are facts in the case that probably only the killer knows and that the police know," Leslie Aaholm said.
Investigators combing through the crime scene at the 15-room home in a posh Boulder neighbourhood were expected to wrap up their work by Saturday morning.

Between 30 and 40 members of the Boulder police department's 125-member staff have been assigned to the case. JonBenet's murder was the only one in Boulder in 1996. In 1995 the town that is home to the University of Colorado had three murder cases, Aaholm said.

Boulder Mayor Leslie Durgin told the briefing from what she knew of the case there was not a murderer stalking the town. "There isn't somebody who is just wandering up and down the streets looking for potential victims," she said, citing published reports there was no forced entry into the Ramsey home.

The Ramseys arrived back in the Denver area on Friday morning by privately chartered jet and Boulder police were attempting to set up a formal interview, Aaholm said, most likely with their attorneys present.

On New Year's Day, the Ramseys appeared on Cable News Network and denied any involvement in the murder and offered a $50,000 reward for information on their daughter's killer. Also in the CNN interview the Ramseys said they planned to assemble a private investigative team to ferret out clues. Patricia Ramsey said tearfully there was "killer on the loose" in Boulder.
